headline: 10 tourists killed in Cox’s Bazar resort fire
summary: The Tup-tup resort in Inani lacked a fire safety license and had been warned by authorities in June.
details: At least 10 tourists were killed and 7 others injured in a devastating fire at the Tup-Tup Resort in the Patuartaek area of Inani, Cox's Bazar.
The fire broke out on Saturday morning around 7:25 AM. Firefighters from the Ukhiya fire station arrived at the scene after a 30-minute journey, starting rescue operations at 8:00 AM.
Two units of the Ukhiya fire service worked for 50 minutes to bring the blaze under control, and the fire was completely extinguished by 11:00 AM.
Rescue teams recovered 10 bodies from the ruins of the resort. The injured victims are currently receiving treatment at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital.
Brigadier General Sultanul Afrin Junaid, Director General of the Fire Service and Civil Defence, confirmed that the resort lacked a fire safety license.
The Fire Service had previously warned the resort authorities about the lack of safety measures in June of this year.
A five-member investigation committee, led by the district magistrate, has been formed by the district administration to determine the cause of the fire and the total loss.
caption:
10 tourists killed in a resort fire in Cox's Bazar. The resort had no fire safety license and had been previously warned.

At least 10 tourists were killed and 7 others injured in a devastating fire at the Tup-Tup Resort in the Patuartaek area of Inani, Cox's Bazar.

The fire broke out on Saturday morning around 7:25 AM. Firefighters from the Ukhiya fire station arrived at the scene after a 30-minute journey, starting rescue operations at 8:00 AM.

Two units of the Ukhiya fire service worked for 50 minutes to bring the blaze under control, and the fire was completely extinguished by 11:00 AM.

Rescue teams recovered 10 bodies from the ruins of the resort. The injured victims are currently receiving treatment at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital.

Brigadier General Sultanul Afrin Junaid, Director General of the Fire Service and Civil Defence, confirmed that the resort lacked a fire safety license.

The Fire Service had previously warned the resort authorities about the lack of safety measures in June of this year.

A five-member investigation committee, led by the district magistrate, has been formed by the district administration to determine the cause of the fire and the total loss.

headline_marked: Doctor [[suspended after PM catches him smoking]] in hospital room
headline: Doctor suspended after PM catches him smoking in hospital room
summary: Associate Professor Rafiqul Islam of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital was suspended following a surprise visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman ordered immediate action against a doctor at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute in Agargaon after finding him smoking in his room during a surprise visit.
Following the directive, Associate Professor Rafiqul Islam was suspended. The Prime Minister expressed strong displeasure, noting that the doctor's room was also in an unhygienic condition.
During the visit, the Prime Minister inspected various departments to assess the working environment for health workers and the overall cleanliness of the facility.
Tarique Rahman instructed the chairman of the hospital's management board, Professor Dr AKM Azizul Haque, to take action against the doctor for the violation.
The Prime Minister stressed the necessity of maintaining a hygienic environment and urged doctors and staff to be more responsible in their duties.
The visit was part of a series of surprise inspections of hospitals and educational institutions in the capital to assess the dengue situation and cleanliness activities.
caption:
A surprise visit by the Prime Minister leads to the immediate suspension of a doctor caught smoking in a hospital room.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman ordered immediate action against a doctor at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute in Agargaon after finding him smoking in his room during a surprise visit.

Following the directive, Associate Professor Rafiqul Islam was suspended. The Prime Minister expressed strong displeasure, noting that the doctor's room was also in an unhygienic condition.

During the visit, the Prime Minister inspected various departments to assess the working environment for health workers and the overall cleanliness of the facility.

Tarique Rahman instructed the chairman of the hospital's management board, Professor Dr AKM Azizul Haque, to take action against the doctor for the violation.

The Prime Minister stressed the necessity of maintaining a hygienic environment and urged doctors and staff to be more responsible in their duties.

The visit was part of a series of surprise inspections of hospitals and educational institutions in the capital to assess the dengue situation and cleanliness activities.
